newsitem.title: USA: Activists press Greyhound to make buses accessible.
newsitem.headline: Activists press Greyhound to make buses accessible.

text.p: About 60 activists protesting a lack of wheelchair lifts on Greyhound buses took over stairwells and hallways of the company's Dallas headquarters on Friday, company officials said.

Members of American Disabled for Attendant Programs Today, or ADAPT, many in wheelchairs, staged simultaneous protests at bus stations in Denver, Houston and other cities to press the company to make its 2,000 inter-city buses accessible to the handicapped.

"They are protesting what they believe to be unfair business practices by Greyhound. They want us to install a wheelchair lift on every bus in our fleet," Greyhound Lines spokeswoman Katherine Williams said.

Protesters said the lack of lifts nationwide made it impossible for a wheelchair-bound passenger to travel across the country. Wheelchair lifts are being tested on six Greyhound buses, but not all stations are equipped to assist wheelchair-bound passengers.
Greyhound said it is in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, which among other things requires transit companies to make their buses accessible to the handicapped.
Police were called to Greyhound's headquarters in suburban Dallas but there had been no arrests, Williams said.
